task: Make the smoke quote a merge to main needs, and land with it
do: On the branch: `git merge origin/main` and commit (the head must contain main: the quote names the head's tree, which a --no-ff merge keeps). Build that commit's release blaze on blaze-vm and, in that checkout, run `blaze run -q -p scripts --bin smoke -- '{"blaze": "/root/inst/blaze", "work": "/root/wt/<lane>/smoke"}' > smoke.txt` inside the same `/root/loop.sh` call (work must be absent or empty; add `"projects": ["hello", "six"]` for the six-crate fixture). Exit 0 only for `verdict ok`; on a failure, standard error has the failed step's output tail, `<work>/<project>-home/v2/serve.log`'s tail and the slowest spans of the last build, and every step's logs are in `<work>/logs/`. Copy smoke.txt to the Mac and run `python3 .github/scripts/land.py '{"what": "what the branch does", "smoke": "smoke.txt"}'`: it checks the quote against `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` with `smoke '{"verify": {"quote": ..., "tree": ...}}'`, puts it in the pull request's body, and its waiting checks it again before it merges. When main moves past the head before the merge, merge main again and make a new quote: the old one names a tree that will not be main.
why: Rule proof-before-merge: on 2026-11-13 three pull requests were admin-merged on compile checks and the merged blaze segfaulted at start, then could not finish a cold hello-world. land.py now refuses without the quote, and there is no flag around it.
